The NEC-Basic Scattering Code is a user-oriented computer code.
The code uses the Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (GTD) to simulate complex structures.
The code can simulate flat plates, infinite ground planes, and finite elliptic cylinders.
Each plate should have edges at least a wavelength long.
The major and minor radii and length of the finite elliptic cylinder should be a wavelength in extent.
The source distribution is a dipole source or an aperture source.
The far-zone electric field equation is given by E(θ,φ) = Eo(A)Fx(ep - jrk 'r')/r.
The GTD diffraction coefficients are designed to smooth out discontinuities in the fields.
The shadowing process is used to determine if a ray path is interrupted by any structure along the complete ray path.
The importance of the neglected terms is determined by the size of the so-called glitches or jumps in the pattern trace.
The NEC-Basic Scattering Code has been interfaced with the Moment Method code.
The Code Manual provides detailed information about the FORTRAN coding.
The code is designed to be efficient and accurate, with a focus on high-frequency analysis.
The code can simulate antennas in the presence of perfectly conducting metal structures at UHF and above.
The code can simulate arbitrary antenna shapes and sizes.
The code can simulate arbitrary source distributions.
The code can simulate arbitrary observation directions.
